summary: The previous concurrency bound still uses an optimistic legacy rate and displays conflicting rate units; the reopened report is not fixed on the default branch.
currentBehavior: The default branch projects about 80 queue completions per minute for the reported settings. The durable worker sends two calls per batch and waits for a five-second idle poll, matching the screenshots showing 144 dequeues over six minutes (24/minute). A tested branch patch includes that cadence and corrects the displayed units.
resolution: Review and release the worker-aware estimate patch, then compare its displayed queue finish range with a real campaign before closing.
rootCause: The old 200ms queue-next plus 500ms webhook-delay heuristic assumes 1.43 dial starts per second. Durable dispatch now schedules a successor one second after each batch; an idle worker sleeps five seconds before claiming it. The concurrency-only patch did not model that loop. The UI also appends calls/sec and CPS to values already converted to per minute. Remaining queue counts are correct; no arbitrary duration multiplier or worker pacing change is needed.
existingTests: test/worker.test.ts: real poll loop with fake time proves a one-second successor waits five seconds.
test/campaign-outbound-estimate.test.ts: 24/minute cadence, stable projected average finish for both reported screenshot counts, configured-rate and concurrency controls.
test/ui/campaign-launch-ivr-estimate.test.tsx: real notice renders calls/minute, worker pacing and remaining-queue wording.
missingTests: After release, compare the displayed range with an actual campaign; the estimate is a planning model and provider/database delays can vary.
acceptanceCriteria: Default planning rate includes the durable worker batch and poll cadence.
The two reported queue counts keep the average projected finish stable at the reported processing pace.
Rate labels use consistent units and distinguish a drained queue from calls still in flight.
A deployed campaign confirms the estimate is useful before closing.
trackerRecommendation: Keep open in progress for review, release and deployed acceptance. The prior master concurrency-only fix is insufficient; remove the old verify-and-close claim.

summary: POST /api/contact-form is a public, unauthenticated multipart route: the route module re-exports the action (app/routes/api+/contact-form.tsx:1), the path is in scripts/baselines/route-tree.txt:68, and the repository's own API surface…
currentBehavior: POST /api/contact-form is a public, unauthenticated multipart route: the route module re-exports the action (app/routes/api+/contact-form.tsx:1), the path is in scripts/baselines/route-tree.txt:68, and the repository's own API surface inventory lists it as publicUnauthenticated (docs/api-surface-inventory.md:64). The action reads the body with await request.formData() at app/routes/api+/contact-form.action.server.ts:36 - no byte cap - before any of its own field limits run. An anonymous multipart POST carrying a 32 MiB body made the shared web process grow by 64.5 MiB of resident memory inside the request (measured: 202.4 MiB -> 270.1 MiB peak RSS, still 269.5 MiB after a forced GC), and…
rootCause: The request-body size check this codebase already implements as app/lib/bounded-form-data.server.ts#readBoundedFormData was applied only to the media upload surfaces. Every other multipart route under app/routes/api+ calls the platform's request.formData() directly, which reads the entire body into process memory before any field validation runs, so the bytes one caller can make the shared web process hold are bounded only by the transport's own per-request default (Bun's 128 MB, node_modules/bun-types/serve.d.ts:676, not overridden at server/bun.ts:357) and by nothing at all in aggregate.
resolution: Read every request body through the reader this codebase already has. Replace each direct request.formData() in app/routes/api+ with readBoundedFormData(request, cap) and map FormBodyError to its 413 status, choosing a cap from the route's own field limits (a few tens of KiB for the contact form, a few hundred KiB for survey submissions). Apply the same to the authenticated variants (audiodrop, surveys). As defence in depth, set an explicit maxRequestBodySize on Bun.serve so the transport, not just the handler, bounds a request body; keep it above the largest legitimate body (the media upload cap is 10 MiB + 64 KiB).
existingTests: Bun 1.3.14 in the sandbox (the production Docker image pins oven/bun:1.3.5 and package.json allows bun >=1.2.15). request.formData() over a streamed 32 MiB multipart body: +67.8 MB resident (2.02x body). Real POST /api/contact-form action, 32 MiB body with the honeypot filled: peak RSS 202.4 -> 270.1 MiB (+64.5 MiB,…
missingTests: A regression test for this behaviour fails on the current source and passes with the fix (kill-check: revert the fix and confirm the test goes red).
A negative control for the same path keeps passing, so the fix does not silently widen access.
acceptanceCriteria: A route should read a request body only through a reader that caps the bytes it will consume and rejects an oversized body with 413, so that a field-level limit (MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH, MAX_NAME_LENGTH, a honeypot) bounds the work rather than being validated after the fact. readBoundedFormData(request, maxBytes) already does exactly this and is used by the media surfaces for a ~10 MiB body, with the repository's own test suite (test/bounded-form-data.test.ts) asserting the 413 and the early stream cancellation. The public and authenticated multipart routes should use the same reader with a cap sized for their own fields, and the transport should carry an explicit maxRequestBodySize as a backstop.

The comparison of the two lockfiles shows 250 package names resolving to different version sets (31…

A negative control for the same path keeps passing, so the fix does not silently widen access.
acceptanceCriteria: The drift gate should assert that the dependency tree CI installs and tests (package-lock.json, via `npm ci`) is the same tree the production images install (bun.lock, via `bun install`), so that the artifact which passed install, typecheck, lint and test is the artifact that is deployed. Any divergence between the two resolved trees - including a newer version of a credential-handling dependency landing in only one of them, and a package present in one tree but absent from the other - should fail the build before the image is produced.

recommendedTitle: Workspace-UI recording path stores the take before it measures its duration, and no maximum duration exists anywhere to compare against
summary: POST /workspaces/:id/audios/record normalises the uploaded take with ffmpeg and writes it to the tenant bucket (uploadObject, app/routes/workspaces+/$id/audios/record.action.server.ts:72-81), and only then measures its length with…
currentBehavior: POST /workspaces/:id/audios/record normalises the uploaded take with ffmpeg and writes it to the tenant bucket (uploadObject, app/routes/workspaces+/$id/audios/record.action.server.ts:72-81), and only then measures its length with probeAudioDurationMs (line 84). The measured value is written to workspace_audio.duration_ms and is never compared against a maximum. No maximum-duration constant exists anywhere in the tracked source: a scan of 2525 files across app, shared, server, worker, services, client, scripts, e2e and test found only unrelated string-length caps (Twilio friendly name, IVR hint, audit metadata string, log line, contact message, name, workspace name) and no duration ceiling…
rootCause: The record action's duration handling is a measurement, not a limit: probeAudioDurationMs runs after uploadObject and its return value is only persisted, and no maximum duration is defined or enforced anywhere on the upload/record path, so an arbitrarily long recording is written to durable storage and to the metadata table before anything could reject it.
resolution: Define one maximum recording duration as a shared constant and enforce it before the take is transcoded and before it is stored. Probe the uploaded container with the server's own tool (probeAudioDurationMs) on the raw upload, so an over-long take is rejected with 413 without ever spending ffmpeg time on it and without writing anything to storage; keep the post-transcode measurement for the stored metadata. Have the browser recorder stop at the same maximum, and keep the ffmpeg wall-clock guard consistent with the maximum rather than relying on it as the policy.
existingTests: The request returned 302 with Location /workspaces/<workspaceId>/audios/recorded-<stamp>.mp3/edit, the normalised object was PUT to the bucket (8279 bytes), and workspace_audio held a row with file_name 'recorded-<stamp>.mp3', origin 'recording', duration_ms 14266340 (3.96 hours), size_bytes 8279, content_type…
missingTests: A regression test for this behaviour fails on the current source and passes with the fix (kill-check: revert the fix and confirm the test goes red).
A negative control for the same path keeps passing, so the fix does not silently widen access.
acceptanceCriteria: A recording is bounded in duration before it is transcoded and before it is stored. The server already measures every recording with its own probe (probeAudioDurationMs), specifically so the recorded length is the server's own measurement rather than the client's timer, and the client already sends a durationMs field; that measured length is expected to be checked against a maximum, with the request rejected before the object is written, and the browser recorder expected to stop at the same maximum.

summary: IVR voicemail drops start during the greeting and a valid machine-end result can hang up without leaving the saved message.
currentBehavior: The default branch still requests early Enable detection. PR #3005 into dev waits for the greeting when a playable drop is configured and recognizes all documented machine-end results. It is open; no live voicemail recording has been verified.
resolution: Review and deploy PR #3005, then verify the complete recorded message with an approved test recipient before closing.
rootCause: Twilio Enable returns machine_start while the greeting is still playing. The fixed one-second pause cannot wait for that greeting. The previous substring classifier also excluded machine_end_other, which Twilio documents as a machine result. Regression tests reproduced both code defects before the patch.
